clue.text: Paper tossed around Church Times newspaper, following brief talk

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the word for talk loses its final letter
following tells us the newspaper pieces come after the shortened talk word

parts.note: CONFER means to talk; cut short it loses its R
T is time, so times in the plural is two of them
the i is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone at the Church Times flings the paper about after a quick chat.
explanation.walkthrough: Church Times looks like the name of a paper, but Church belongs to the definition: the paper thrown about outside a church at weddings.
explanation.definitionFit: Confetti is the shower of small paper pieces thrown over a bride and groom outside the church.

clue.text: Player needing racket before match with six-footer

indicators.note: before sets the racket word ahead of the following pieces

parts.note: a racket is a swindle, a con
a Test is an international cricket match
an insect has six legs

explanation.surface: A tennis player needs a racquet before a game against a very tall opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: Six-footer suggests a tall person; it is an insect with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A contestant is anyone taking part in a game or competition, a participant.

clue.text: Unpleasant feeling rising, changing side of street

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from bottom to top
changing means one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: an emotion is a feeling
street is ST, and changing its side swaps the T for the S

explanation.surface: A nasty sentiment grows as someone crosses the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Street is ST; changing side turns its T into S, so the reversed feeling has its T replaced by S.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disgusting, especially of a smell, so thoroughly unpleasant.

clue.text: 'Great score of course — I'd sounded sharp

parts.note: an eagle is two under par on a golf course

indicators.note: sounded means spoken, so we want a word that is said the same way

parts.note: the contraction is said like a word meaning looked at

explanation.surface: A golfer remarks that a fine score came as no surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Of course hides a golf course rather than meaning naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eagle-eyed has keen sight and notices fine detail, so is observant.

clue.text: Mickey Mouse beat Dumbo up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from the bottom

parts.note: to top is to beat or outdo
a dumbo is a fool, a nit

explanation.surface: One Disney cartoon character thrashes another.
explanation.walkthrough: Mickey Mouse and Dumbo look like a Disney pair; the first is British slang for amateurish.
explanation.definitionFit: Mickey Mouse as an adjective means trivial or amateurish, the same as tinpot.

clue.text: Feast that might accompany toast?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lavish meal laid out for guests
second meaning: butter, jam or paste put on bread

explanation.surface: A banquet at which speeches and toasts are raised.
explanation.walkthrough: Toast suggests raising a glass at a feast; here it is grilled bread, with something smeared on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a big meal set out on a table and a soft food like butter or jam for bread.

clue.text: Force constituent to accept an island state

indicators.note: to accept means taking something in, so the officer holds the next letters

parts.note: a police constable is a member of the force
taken as written
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A member of a federation is made to admit an island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks like a country, but it is a state of mind; force is the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is a state of sudden overwhelming fear, a condition someone is in.

clue.text: Medicine struggles to eliminate one?

indicators.note: something that struggles writhes about, so the letters are thrown out of order
to eliminate means to remove, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Doctors fight to wipe out a disease.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes an endemic disease, one that stays in a population however hard medicine tries.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic disease is permanently present in a region, which is why treatment struggles to wipe it out.

clue.text: Kinks's Ray or Dave losing fight for unknown song of theirs?

indicators.note: losing one thing for another means swapping it out for a replacement

parts.note: Ray and Dave Davies were the brothers who led the Kinks
to vie is to compete or fight
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: One of the Kinks' brothers abandons a quarrel over an obscure track.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kinks were a 1960s British rock band; Days is one of their singles, from 1968.
explanation.definitionFit: Days is a 1968 single by the Kinks, so a song by the band named in the clue.

clue.text: Want beans cooked this time

indicators.note: cooked food has been worked over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
CE is Common Era, the present dating system

explanation.surface: Someone fancies beans prepared for a meal on this occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: Want looks like a verb for desire; here it is the noun for lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of lack or shortage matches absence, as in for want of evidence.

clue.text: Tool turned fruit into bread

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the fruit is read from its end back to its start
into means the turned fruit is placed inside the bread

parts.note: naan or nan is a flat Indian bread
the ugli is a citrus fruit, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Fruit was baked into a loaf by some instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail gun is a power tool that drives nails into wood with compressed air.

clue.text: Very crisp, black, straight lines

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black on pencils
a straight line is one-dimensional, written 1-D
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A description of something very crisp: black with straight lines, like a design.
explanation.walkthrough: The reading of straight as one-D is the setter's stretch: a straight line has only one dimension.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bone-dry has no moisture left at all, so toast or leaves in that state are extremely crisp.

clue.text: Call up First Lady without consent

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the first lady wraps around the consent

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
OK is a word of agreement

explanation.surface: A president's wife is summoned without her agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Without seems to mean lacking, but here it means outside. First Lady suggests a president's wife; it is Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a memory or feeling is to summon it to mind, the same as calling it up.

clue.text: Discover comedian's middle eight moved significantly

indicators.note: middle eight asks for the eight letters at the centre of the words just before it

parts.note: the central eight letters of these two words run together

explanation.surface: A music fan finds that a comedian's song bridge was deeply touching.
explanation.walkthrough: Middle eight sounds like the bridge section of a pop song; here it counts out the eight central letters of discover comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overcome is to be overwhelmed by strong emotion, which is to be deeply moved.

clue.text: I'm avoiding outside excursion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the mark in the contraction stands where a letter was left out
second meaning: in rhetoric, a turning aside to address someone not present

explanation.walkthrough: In I'm the mark replaces the missing A of am. The rhetorical figure is a digression in which a speaker addresses someone absent, an excursion to the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the punctuation mark showing an omission and a speech's digression addressing an absent person.

clue.text: T-shirt design represented Eastern deity

indicators.note: represented means shown again in a new form, so these letters are set out afresh

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east or eastern
taken as written

explanation.surface: A god from the East printed on a T-shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Tie-dye is a method of colouring fabric in swirls, a familiar pattern on hippie-style T-shirts.

clue.text: What seals second team appearance

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a crew is a team, as of rowers
a cap is an appearance for a national side

explanation.surface: A sports report on what clinches a reserve side's game.
explanation.walkthrough: A cap is awarded for each match played for one's country, so it stands for an appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw cap is a threaded lid that closes a bottle or jar tightly.

clue.text: Ceremony of religious leader touring America after several other countries

indicators.note: after places the leader and country pieces behind the group of countries

parts.note: the European Union is a group of countries

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the leader goes around the country letter

parts.note: the founder of Christianity
A is the abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: A ritual held for a church leader on a tour of the US after visiting other nations.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eucharist is the Christian sacrament of Holy Communion, a religious rite.

clue.text: Student article that's cutting edge

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the article sits inside the edge word

parts.note: a border is an edge
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A student's essay that is at the forefront of thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: Cutting edge reads as one phrase meaning innovative; cutting is the container signal and edge the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: A boarder is a pupil who lives at their school during term.

clue.text: Oxen trod precariously close

indicators.note: something done precariously is unstable and liable to topple, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cattle stepped dangerously near a cliff edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Next door, used as an adjective or adverb, means immediately adjacent, so very near.

clue.text: Vote in favour of keeping Move It

parts.note: a cross marks a vote on a ballot paper

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so the favour word holds the next one inside

parts.note: for means supporting
to move is to take action, to act

explanation.surface: A call to back the old Cliff Richard hit Move It on a TV talent show.
explanation.walkthrough: Move It looks like a song title; It is the definition. The X Factor was also a British TV talent show.
explanation.definitionFit: Both it and the X factor mean an indefinable quality of special appeal or star charisma.

clue.text: Legendary winger is engaging about sport

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the two-letter word holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: taken as written
CA is short for circa, about
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A famed rugby wing player gets involved in talk about the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Winger looks like a rugby position; it means one with wings. Icarus flew on wax wings too near the sun in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Icarus is the mythical youth who flew on wings his father Daedalus made, so a winged figure of legend.

clue.text: Degenerate left church area after religious teaching

indicators.note: after places the left and church area pieces behind the teaching

parts.note: RE is religious education in schools
L is the abbreviation for left
the apse is the rounded end of a church

explanation.surface: A wicked person walked out of church after a sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: Degenerate looks like a noun for a reprobate, but it is the verb: to get worse.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to fall back into a worse condition, which is to deteriorate.

clue.text: Rock and roll's first book penned by Jack or Tom?

indicators.note: penned by means shut inside, so the letters go inside the next word

parts.note: a jack and a tom are male animals

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A rock and roll guide written by a man called Jack or Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock and roll reads as one phrase, but Rock is the definition and only roll feeds the wordplay. Jack and Tom are male animals, a jack donkey and a tom cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Marble is a hard metamorphic rock used in sculpture and building.

clue.text: Australian site may make a typo, e.g. in fliers

parts.note: can, like may, says something is possible

indicators.note: in places the error word inside the word for the fliers

parts.note: BA is British Airways
a typo is an example of making a mistake

explanation.surface: An Australian website may print mistakes, for instance on its flyers.
explanation.walkthrough: Site suggests a website; it is the place where the capital stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Canberra is the capital city of Australia, a location in that country.

clue.text: S African gathering support over Grok, say

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the support word above the next piece

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
Grok is an artificial intelligence chatbot

explanation.surface: A South African meeting backs the Grok chatbot.
explanation.definitionFit: A braai is the South African word for a barbecue and the social get-together around it.

clue.text: Conan Doyle character's superlative conclusion leaving Lestrade confused

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the remaining letters are jumbled
leaving means departing from, so those letters are taken out of the inspector's name

parts.note: the ending of superlatives such as biggest
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Sherlock Holmes character's brilliant ending baffles Inspector Lestrade.
explanation.walkthrough: Lestrade minus the letters of the superlative suffix leaves five letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene Adler is the woman who outwits Holmes in Conan Doyle's story A Scandal in Bohemia.

clue.text: Bag of chopped beef

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a beef is a complaint, a gripe

explanation.surface: A bag of minced beef from the butcher.
explanation.walkthrough: Beef looks like meat, but it is slang for a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A grip is an old word for a travelling bag or holdall.

clue.text: Gunners locate treadmill

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
to trace something is to find it

explanation.surface: Arsenal players find a piece of gym equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Gunners suggests Arsenal football club; in crosswords it is the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are figurative names for a dull, competitive and endless routine of work.

clue.text: Slowing down quietly during dance music from the 90s

indicators.note: during places the musical pieces within the dance word

parts.note: to bop is to dance
rit. is ritardando, the score marking for slowing
p is piano, softly, in music

explanation.surface: A song's tempo drops softly while people dance in a 90s club.
explanation.definitionFit: Britpop was the guitar-led British pop movement of bands like Oasis and Blur in the mid-1990s.

clue.text: A university grant

parts.note: a, as in five pounds a day, means per
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A college's funding award.
explanation.walkthrough: Grant looks like a noun for student funding, but it is the verb: to allow.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit something is to allow it, which is one sense of the verb to grant.

clue.text: Art lover hates high summer in Paris

indicators.note: high as in intoxicated, so those letters are out of their senses and reordered

parts.note: taken as written
été is French for summer

explanation.surface: A culture vulture loathes the height of the season in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: High summer reads as one phrase, but high is the anagram signal and summer goes into French.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is someone with a refined appreciation of beauty, especially in art.
